text:
Maureen (People Ops): Quick follow-up from today's leadership Q&A — putting clarifications here about the year-end review tie-break rules, comp timing, and 401k/benefits windows. I'll update the handbook after this thread.
Priya G: Thanks — first: if two people end up with the same rating and one manager pushes for promotion while the other doesn't, how do you break ties for limited promo slots?
Maureen (People Ops): Good Q. Tie-breakers go: 1) manager recommendation + documented impact, 2) calibration notes + peer feedback quality, 3) time-in-role and readiness signals, 4) org prioritization (skill gaps / product needs). We try to avoid arbitrary lotteries.
Jordan L: For merit increases approved in the Nov comp committee, when do they hit paychecks? Any retro pay?
Maureen (People Ops): Merit increases are effective Dec 1 and appear on the Dec payroll. We don't do multi-month retro pay for standard cycles — exceptions only for documented HR errors, handled case-by-case. Payroll cut-off is noted below.
Sasha: Is there any change to 401k matching or the enrollment window this year? Deadline?
Maureen (People Ops): No change to the match rate this year (still 4% up to 6% eligible match policy). Open enrollment for benefits and 401k adjustments is Nov 15 — Dec 15. Changes made in that window are reflected in the first paycheck after Jan 1 for pre-tax elections; employer match contributions follow the plan schedule. Catch-up and FSA/HSA rules unchanged.
Ravi K: If an IC thinks their rating is inaccurate, what's the appeals timeline and who reviews?
Maureen (People Ops): Start with manager discussion. If unresolved, file an appeal with People Ops within 30 days of the final rating notification. Appeals route: manager -> people ops intake -> compensation committee review (if needed). We aim to conclude appeals within 21 business days. Note: appeals can change rating and comp decisions but any comp changes still follow payroll schedules.
Payroll Bot: Reminder: payroll change cut-off for Dec cycle is 2126001200 (Nov 20 11:59pm PT). Salary change forms must be submitted before cut-off to affect Dec 1 pay.
Priya G: Appreciate the specifics — can you post the short timeline snippet so managers can forward it to teams? :thumbsup:
Maureen (People Ops): Sure — posting quick copyable timeline below. I'll paste this into the handbook and the manager playbook.
Maureen (People Ops): ```
Review & comp timeline (copy for teams):
- Oct 10: manager self-reviews due
- Oct 20–Nov 3: manager calibrations
- Nov 4–Nov 10: comp committee reviews
- Nov 20: payroll cut-off for Dec 1 increases
- Dec 1: merit increases effective
- Nov 15–Dec 15: benefits & 401k enrollment window
```
Jordan L: Perfect, will forward to my leads.
Sasha: Quick nit: can we add a one-line about manager documentation standards for promotions (what evidence is enough)?
Maureen (People Ops): Yes — will add a short checklist to the handbook: impact metrics, 3 peer/partner excerpts, growth plan alignment, and manager sign-off. I'll ping when it's live.
Ravi K: Thanks — one last ask: if a promotion is approved after payroll cut-off, is there any retroactive pay option?
Maureen (People Ops): We typically make promotions effective the next payroll cycle. Retroactive pay is rare and only for processing errors; if a promo is approved late due to committee timing we can consider retro for fairness but it requires exec approval and Payroll coordination.
Priya G: Thanks everyone — very clear. Small suggestion: put the handbook link in the follow-up so managers have one click.
Maureen (People Ops): Will do. Posting updated handbook link here when it's live. Thanks all! :sparkles:
